findings.reasoning: The original Latin "DEO LAVDES" (Deo laudes) translates literally as "praises to God" or "praise to God." The modern rendering carries the complete sense of the original: "DEO" (to God) and "LAVDES" (praises/praise). No clauses are omitted, and nothing is added beyond what the original expresses.

The rendering captures all the clauses of the original: (1) "veritas occultatur magno argumento" (truth is hidden by a great argument); (2) "cum ad inquisitionem nostram modicum quid ex parte adversa prolatum sit" (when in response to our inquiry only a small thing is brought forth from the other side); and (3) "cetera sileantur" (the rest is passed over in silence). The structure and sense are preserved in modern English syntax without omission or addition.
